newsitem.title: USA: La.Offshore Oil Port unaffected by U.S. Gulf storm.
newsitem.headline: La.Offshore Oil Port unaffected by U.S. Gulf storm.

text.p: Operation of the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port was unaffected early Thursday by a strengthening tropical depression brewing in the central Gulf of Mexico, a LOOP official said.

"Right now, we don't see any problem," a LOOP dispatcher said of heavy rains and strong winds generated by the storm system. "But if they kick the waves up pretty substantially, we'll move everybody out." The deepwater oil port is located 20 miles south of Grand Isle, La.

Crews on offshore rigs and production platforms were battening down ahead of the system, which buffeted some elevated platforms in the northern Gulf with tropical storm level winds of more than 39 miles an hour overnight.

But so far, only non-essential workers like painters who normally would be brought in during periods of prolonged rain were being ferried back to shore by helicopter as crews prepared to ride out the storm.

"As far as evacuating people, things are quiet. Nobody's done anything," a Petroleum Helicopters Inc dispatcher said. "In some areas, winds are 35 to 40 miles per hour, but that's no problem. They can ride that out."

Texaco removed a dozen workers from offshore platforms on Wednesday and planned to evacuate another 50 on Thursday, and the U.S. Coast Guard received reports overnight from crews shutting in platforms in the Eugene Island section of the Gulf and heading for shore.

The storm was nearly stationary overnight, with satellites and radar pegging its center at latitude 27.8 degrees north, longitude 92.3 degrees west, or about 205 miles southwest of New Orleans. The system was expected to drift to the northeast later today, with the strongest gusts and swells east of the center, the National Hurricane Center in Miami said.
The tropical depression could be upgraded to a tropical storm within 24 hours as maximum sustained winds top 39 miles an hour, forecasters said.
A U.S. Air Force plane was set to fly into the system today. ((--Houston Bureau 713 210-8508))
